messages.author: f04bcd45eb93a866
messages.subject: Simple understanding of STAN syntax
parts:
Hi. I am brand new to STAN. I also have no experience BUGS and JAGS. I have a general understanding of linear models, but I think STAN may open up more possibilities with my modeling abilities. Following the reference manual, I see that a basic linear model can be formed by the following:

diet_code = """

    data {

      int<lower=0> N; //rows of data

      int<lower=0> K; // number of covariates

      matrix[N,K] x; // predictor matrix

      real Y[N]; // response

    }

    parameters {

      vector[K] beta; //intercept and slope parameters

      real<lower=0, upper=100> sigma; // standard deviation

    }

    model {

      // priors

      beta ~ normal(0,100);

      // data model

      Y ~ normal(x * beta, sigma);

    }

    """


This works fine for me. However, I am trying to do a more difficult application, so as a test case I tried the following:


diet_code = """

    data {

      int<lower=0> N; //rows of data

      int<lower=0> K; // number of covariates

      matrix[N,K] x; // predictor matrix

      real Y[N]; // response

      vector[K] Mu;

    }

    parameters {

      vector[K] beta; //intercept and slope parameters

      real<lower=0, upper=100> sigma; // standard deviation

    }

    model {

      // priors

      beta ~ normal(0,100);

      // data model

      Mu <- x * beta;

      Y ~ normal(Mu, sigma);

    }

    """


However, I get the following error:


attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=data

PARSER EXPECTED: <expression assignable to left-hand side>


I obviously have a poor understanding of the syntax. Supposing I wanted to calculate a variable within the model, How would I do this? Thanks.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple understanding of STAN syntax
parts:
What the error message says. You can only define (i.e., assign)
variables in the block in which they were declared.

You can't declare Mu as data (telling Stan to read it in) and
then define it (telling Stan to forget what you read).

You want to define Mu as either a transformed parameter or
as a local variable in the model block, the difference being
that the former will save it.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple understanding of STAN syntax
parts:
(N x K) x (K x 1) = (N x 1)

matrix x vector = vector

Stan reduces types where possible --- the index to
the manual lists all the rules.

It needs to be of size N because it's parallel
to y!

- Bob
